newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WRIGHT OVERCOMES PROBLEMS TO EARN INTERNATIONAL RECALL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WRIGHT OVERCOMES PROBLEMS TO EARN INTERNATIONAL RECALL.

text.p: Goalkeeper Tommy Wright, who considered retiring last year because he had suffered so many injuries, was recalled on Monday to the Northern Ireland squad for next month's World Cup group nine qualifier against Germany.
The 33-year-old Nottingham Forest keeper, who made the last of his 22 international appearances against Mexico two years ago, has come back to form on loan at first division Reading.
"This is a dream. The World Cup match in Germany was the one I was aiming for. Not so long ago I'd have settled for a game in the park on a Saturday. That's how bad things were for me," he said.
"Retirement did cross my mind, I had sufficient medical grounds. But I gave myself a talking to. I love being a professional footballer so I had to do everything to try to carry on.
"Now it's wonderful to get back into my country's international squad."
Manager Bryan Hamilton has also recalled Swindon midfielder Kevin Horlock for the match against the European champions in Nuremberg on November 9.

But midfielders Jim Magilton (Southampton) and Michael O'Neill (Coventry), who came on as substitutes against Armenia last month, have both been left out of the squad because they are not currently in their club sides.
Northern Ireland have made a poor start to their campaign by losing at home to Ukraine and drawing at home with Armenia.
But oddly, they have avoided defeat against Germany on the last four occasions they have met, winning twice and drawing twice since their last defeat in 1977.
Squad (all clubs English except where stated):
Goalkeepers: Alan Fettis (Nottingham Forest), Tommy Wright (Reading)

Defenders: Nigel Worthington (Stoke), Neil Lennon (Leicester), Colin Hill (Leicester), Barry Hunter (Reading), Kevin Horlock (Swindon), Gerry Taggart (Bolton), Danny Griffin (St Johnstone, Scotland), Ian Nolan (Sheffield Wednesday).
Midfield: Keith Rowland (West Ham), Steve Lomas (Manchester City), Steve Morrow (Arsenal), Michael Hughes (West Ham)
Forwards: Keith Gillespie (Newcastle), Iain Dowie (West Ham), Phil Gray (Nancy, France), Gerard McMahon (Stoke)
